description: OMP Desktop patch set for the pinned upstream OMP runtime: RPC host-tool scheduling and batch policy, settle-time run termination, the all-toolCall batch count, a deterministic native-addon archive, and an explicit bytecode switch on the build entry. Risk reduction and release-build reproducibility only: it does NOT make the sole-batch contract strict — see status.

fork.note: Self-maintained fork whose HEAD is exactly base.sha + this patch level. `scripts/omp-sidecar.mjs` refuses any other commit; can1357/oh-my-pi stays a read-only upstream.

contract.invalidDeclaration: set_host_tools request is rejected; the value never degrades to the default
contract.invalidDeclarationDetail: RpcHostToolDefinition.concurrency/batchPolicy values outside their union throw in normalizeHostToolPolicy, which the set_host_tools command and the host-tool adapter both call
contract.bytecodeBuildEntry: packages/coding-agent/scripts/build-binary.ts accepts exactly `--bytecode`/`--no-bytecode` (default on, one declaration, anything else exits 2); `compileCodingAgent` takes it as the typed option `CodingAgentCompileOptions.bytecode`, never from the environment

history.retiredReason: T20-R4-3 added the deterministic native-addon archive and the explicit bytecode build switch, which changed the patched tree; the .2 artifact and its file name are kept in git history, not in this tree.
T20-R4A migrated the patch set to the new pinned base 62bc57be (omp/18.3.0); the 18.2.7 artifact is kept in git history, not in this tree.

notes: This is an OMP Desktop-maintained patch level, not upstream OMP support: the runtime remains pinned at 62bc57be (omp/18.3.0) plus this patch set.

Rebuild the patch after any source edit with: git -C <checkout> -c core.abbrev=7 diff <base.sha> <fork.commit> > app/patches/oh-my-pi/0001-omp-desktop-runtime.patch, then refresh patch.sha256 and patch.bytes. The explicit core.abbrev=7 pins the index lines to 7 hex digits: a machine-level core.abbrev would otherwise change the patch bytes while preserving semantics, so the artifact could not be reproduced byte-for-byte elsewhere.

The patch file was renamed from 0001-rpc-host-tool-transition-contract.patch at .3, when it stopped being only the RPC contract; the current-state documents are updated, the dated validation records keep the name they were written with.

The 18.3.0 artifact is the 18.2.7 artifact with exactly one changed context line: the 18.3.0 agent-loop.ts comment reads `wait` where 18.2.7 read `hub wait`. The added and removed line multisets are identical between the two artifacts.

reproducible-sidecar-build: embed-native.ts writes the embedded addon tar.gz with fixed entry timestamps and a recomputed header checksum, because Bun.Archive stamps each entry with the current time. Without it, two builds of one fork commit produced different binaries — measured at T20-R4-3 on Bun 1.4.2 (first difference at byte 81260680).

explicit-bytecode-build-mode: bytecode stays on by default (upstream release behavior and the fast boot path). The desktop sidecar build passes `--bytecode` explicitly and records it as `build.bytecode` in the provenance manifest; measured reproducibility holds for bytecode on and off once the archive is deterministic.

The .3 patch artifact was regenerated on 2026-10-01 after a comment-only correction of the bytecode documentation in compile-binary.ts and build-binary.ts (fork commit 6226f80…; the superseded fork commit 6b5017bc… and its artifact stay in git history and in the dated R4-3 record). No file in the patch set was added or removed, and no runtime/build behavior changed.

status.blocker: F3: a `kCursorExecResolved` sibling was executed by the provider/editor bridge before the assistant message existed, so its side effect cannot be prevented or retracted by any loop-level patch; PI counts every toolCall block, so the batch is still rejected, but "zero side effects in a rejected batch" is unreachable at this layer.
mitigationsApplied: batch admission counts every toolCall block of the assistant message (Cursor-resolved included), matching PI runtime.ts:2222
speculation is disabled for a provider call whose active tool set advertises a sole-declared tool, so no speculative physical work starts before the batch decision

scopeNote.note: Scope explanation only; it does not change patchLevel, the patch artifact, pins, capability ids or build outputs, and it does not turn the global not-strict fact into a general strict claim. The user excluded the Cursor + Plan/Goal combination from product scope on 2026-10-02: it is unsupported and refused by the ADR 0306 gate, so the F3 blocker above now describes that excluded combination. Non-Cursor providers do not produce the pre-executed blocks, so the non-Cursor route whose dispatch is decided by the patched loop stays in scope and is still held to the strict contract (all-toolCall counting, sole batches, settle-time termination). T20-B/C/D remain unstarted.
